newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Merrill Lynch eyes private banking on Internet.
newsitem.headline: Merrill Lynch eyes private banking on Internet.

text.p: Merrill Lynch Bank hopes to redefine private banking by using Internet to help its clients move their wealth between currencies and countries at the click of a mouse, a top bank official said on Tuesday.

Michael Giles, chairman of Merrill Lynch International Banks London, said his bank was positioning itself to make greater use of the information technology revolution which would play a major role in private banking in the coming years.

"I see utilising the Internet in some capacity to deliver information to our private clients, to communicate with them real-time and to allow them high-level security access to their own accounts," Giles told Reuters during a visit to Zurich.
"We do not have a time frame yet, but we have plans to start doing this."
Giles said a U.S. law dating back to the Cold War era and banning the use of encyrption technology was the only obstacle to using Internet as a new means for private banking.
He said he expected amendments to this law this year to allow banks to use encryption technology needed for protection against computer hackers.

Separately, Giles said Merrill Lynch would invest a total of $60 million in a new computer system to help private banking relationship managers offer better services and improve database management and productivity.

"Technology is going to be extremely important in the private banking business," he said. "That is absolutely going to be necessary because of globalisation, the emergence of new markets around the world and increasing client education and sophistication."

In the first such service of its kind in Switzerland's private banking industry, a Geneva-based company has already started benchmarking asset management services and offering them to clients by using Internet-type technology.

NatioVision, owned 51 percent by French Banque Nationale de Paris, says it is providing data, television images, analysis, stock and foreign exchange market information from third parties to private banking clients on a real-time basis.
